weaknesses: The added Monday and Tuesday Solo Editing Overflow blocks create an uninterrupted visible work/performance stretch from 12:30 to 23:30 on both days: existing Video Editing Block 12:30-18:00, added Solo Editing Overflow 18:00-20:00, and Live Stream 20:00-23:30. The rationale treats the 18:00-20:00 gaps as available capacity but does not address the practical loss of the only visible pre-stream recovery, meal, setup, or transition window on those days.

The proposal preserves sleep and gym, which is positive, but it underweighs cumulative load across the visible week: daily Gym Workout 10:00-11:30, long editing blocks on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, nightly Live Streams 20:00-23:30, and a fixed Wednesday guest recording 14:00-17:00. The added blocks intensify the two already-heavy opening days rather than demonstrating why that concentration is sustainable.

The rationale rejects late-night editing as less protective of recovery, but it does not compare that recovery concern against the recovery and preparation cost of working directly into the 20:00 streams. Avoiding late-night work is reasonable, yet the chosen placement still compresses evening needs.

Alternatives are considered at a high level, but they focus mostly on avoiding disruption to streams and fixed events. They do not show whether a lighter distribution, shorter overflow, or use of less compressed visible gaps was considered within the same calendar horizon.

Request satisfaction cannot be verified from the provided material. The proposal refers to a requested catch-up and Wednesday afternoon being occupied, but the actual amount of needed overflow work and deadline pressure are not visible.
critic_evaluation.feedback: The plan is technically clean and avoids moving fixed or participant-facing events, but its human manageability is only partly supported. The main concern is not that the added events overlap anything; it is that Monday and Tuesday become dense production days with no visible break from 12:30 to 23:30 before repeating similar obligations later in the week. The Proposer should reconsider whether using both 18:00-20:00 gaps is proportionate to the catch-up need, or provide grounded context showing how meals, stream preparation, cognitive recovery, and breaks are handled within the existing blocks. A revision could still keep the same operations if the fuller context supports them, but the current rationale does not sufficiently justify the sustainability of the added load.

plausibility_review.reason: The proposed additions materially reduce practical recovery and preparation margin on Monday and Tuesday by extending existing 12:30-18:00 editing directly into 20:00-23:30 streams. This could affect stream quality, fatigue, food timing, and the sustainability of the visible week, especially with daily gym sessions and further production/streaming commitments through Friday. The issue is plausible rather than objectively impossible, because breaks may exist within flexible work blocks, but the current rationale does not substantiate that.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Reconsider the distribution or intensity of the overflow work using the fuller context, or explicitly justify how the user can manage meals, transition, stream preparation, and recovery on Monday and Tuesday despite the continuous 12:30-23:30 visible workload.
